title: Not by instruction: by the one he chooses
theme: This self is not attained by instruction, nor by intelligence, nor by much learning; by the one whom he chooses is he attained; to him this self reveals its own form.

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: a + a → ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः); final m stays before a vowel.
aḥ → o before n, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च).

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi; eṣaḥ before a consonant
sandhi.rule: Final m stays before a vowel; a + e → ai, P. 6.1.88 (वृद्धिरेचि); eṣaḥ loses its visarga before a consonant, P. 6.1.132 (एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि).

sandhi.type: visarga before t; vowel sandhi; eṣaḥ before a vowel
sandhi.rule: Visarga before t becomes s, P. 8.3.34 (विसर्जनीयस्य सः); a + e → ai, P. 6.1.88 (वृद्धिरेचि); before a vowel the visarga of eṣaḥ becomes y, P. 8.3.17 (भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि), and is dropped, P. 8.3.19 (लोपः शाकल्यस्य); the hiatus stays.
Final m → anusvāra before a consonant, P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः); the base writes the two words without a space.

morphology.note: Present middle of vṛ (class 5, vṛṇoti / vṛṇute) ‘choose’; the same verb with vi- in विवृणुते means ‘uncover, open’. The verse plays on the two: the one chosen (vṛṇute) is the one to whom the self opens (vivṛṇute).
Gerundive of labh ‘obtain’ in -ya: ‘to be obtained, attainable’; Śaṅkara glosses ‘to be known’.
tanū ‘body, form, person’; here, with स्वाम्, the self’s ‘own form’ — Śaṅkara: its true nature.

translation.literal: ‘This self is not to be attained by instruction, not by intelligence, not by much learning. Whom alone this one chooses, by him [it] is to be attained; to him this self uncovers its own form.’
translation.readable: ‘This self is not won by teaching, nor by cleverness, nor by much learning. It is won by the one it chooses; to that one the self reveals its own true form.’

anvaya: अयम् आत्मा न प्रवचनेन लभ्यः न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । एषः यम् एव वृणुते तेन लभ्यः । तस्य एषः आत्मा स्वाम् तनूम् विवृणुते ॥
syntax: Three negated instrumentals (pravacanena, medhayā, bahunā śrutena) with labhyaḥ, then a correlative pair yam … tena: ‘whom he chooses, by him [it is] attainable’, and a closing sentence with tasya … vivṛṇute. The subject of vṛṇute, eṣaḥ, is not specified — the crux of the verse.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: the seeker chooses the self — his own self — and by that self alone is it attained: «यमेव स्वमात्मानम् एष साधको वृणुते प्रार्थयते», «आत्मनैवात्मा लभ्यत इत्यर्थः». Raṅgarāmānuja: the Supreme chooses the seeker: «एषः - परमात्मा», «साधकं प्रार्थयते», and the one chosen is the one most dear to him. Madhva, in our source, does not comment on this verse.

ambiguities.topic: pravacana — teaching others, or one’s own reflection?
ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: taking up many Vedas, «अनेकवेदस्वीकरणेन». Raṅgarāmānuja, following Vyāsārya: reflection, «प्रवचनं मननम्», since teaching others could not be thought a means at all.
Raṅgarāmānuja knows a reading vṛṇute in the last line and says the sense is the same, «वृणुते इति पाठेऽपि स एवार्थः». None of our witnesses has it.

metre.name: triṣṭubh
metre.note: Counted as written, 22 and 23 syllables: the last pāda, tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām, has twelve because eṣa ātmā stays in hiatus.

beginner: This is one of the best-known verses in the Upaniṣads, and the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad repeats it word for word. The self cannot be gained by lectures, by sharp intelligence, or by having read a great deal. It is gained by the one whom it chooses, and to that person it shows its true form. But who does the choosing? The Sanskrit leaves it open, and the traditions divide here. Śaṅkara says the seeker chooses: whoever longs for the self alone, and nothing else, finds that the self reveals itself, so the self is reached through the self. Raṅgarāmānuja says the Lord chooses: he chooses the person who loves him, and the worshipper's love awakens the Lord's love in return. Either way, cleverness alone is not enough.
analogy: Like friendship: no amount of research about a person makes them your friend; at some point they must open the door.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: That the self is not attained by instruction, intelligence or learning, but by the one whom ‘this one’ chooses, and that to him the self reveals its own form.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The seeker, who chooses his own self: «यमेव स्वमात्मानम् एष साधको वृणुते प्रार्थयते». By that self, the chooser, the self is attained: «तेनैवात्मना वरित्रा स्वयमात्मा लभ्यः». One without desire asks for the self alone, «निष्कामश्चात्मानमेव प्रार्थयते», and the self reveals its own true nature, «पारमार्थिकीं स्वां तनूं».

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: The Supreme chooses the seeker, «साधकं प्रार्थयते», and is attainable by the one he chooses, «प्रार्थनीयपुंसा लभ्यः». Only the one dearest to him is so chosen, and he is dearest who loves him: the worshipper’s love for the Lord produces the Lord’s love for him, which brings attainment, «भगवतः उपासके प्रीतिमुत्पाद्य तत्प्राप्तिहेतुः भवतीत्यर्थः». Then the Supreme gives himself, «स्वात्मानं प्रयच्छति».

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: Not in our source: Madhva gives this verse without comment, and his mūla keys pravacena (a dropped syllable) for pravacanena (corrections.json, witness-error). The vishvAsa mūla writes labhyaḥ tasyaiṣa with the visarga (orthographic).

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: The Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad has it word for word (3.2.3) and follows it with a verse of its own on the same theme: not by one lacking strength, nor through negligence (3.2.4).

advaita.text: The chooser is the seeker, the chosen his own self; the self is attained by the self alone: «आत्मनैवात्मा लभ्यत इत्यर्थः». Learning without that desire for the self does not reach it.

visistadvaita.text: The chooser is the Supreme, the chosen the seeker who loves him; the worshipper’s love awakens the Lord’s, «भगवतः उपासके प्रीतिमुत्पाद्य तत्प्राप्तिहेतुः भवतीत्यर्थः», and the Lord then reveals and gives himself.

schools.disagreement: Śaṅkara makes the seeker the chooser and the self the chosen: attainment is the self’s self-disclosure to one who wants nothing else. Raṅgarāmānuja makes the Lord the chooser and the loving worshipper the chosen: attainment is by divine choice answering love. Madhva’s bhāṣya, in our source, is silent on the verse.

parallels.quote: यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम्
parallels.note: The Muṇḍaka repeats the whole verse.
The Muṇḍaka’s next verse continues the series of negations with strength, care and austerity.

contemporary.text: Credentials, reading and intelligence are real goods, and the verse does not despise them; it says they are not sufficient. Many people who have learned something deeply say that it was given as much as earned. (A modern reflection.)

reflect.beginner: What have you understood that no amount of reading could have given you?
reflect.deeper: If the seeker chooses (Śaṅkara), what is the role of grace? If the Lord chooses (Raṅgarāmānuja), what is the role of effort?
reflect.practice: Choose one question you care about and, for a week, return to it daily without looking anything up.

references.text: Raṅgarāmānuja follows Vyāsārya on the meaning of pravacana; this is reported as cited by him.

flags.note: The verse does not name the subject of vṛṇute; whether it is the seeker (Śaṅkara) or the Supreme (Raṅgarāmānuja) is the central point on which the schools part.
Madhva’s digital text keys pravacena for pravacanena (corrections.json, witness-error).
